correctness.rationale: The direct finite proof is complete for the claimed bounded range: a connected trivially perfect graph is uniquely a rooted-tree ancestor graph; the multiset-of-children generator enumerates all such trees through 16 vertices (376,464 classes). The exact domination recurrence checks every coefficient using integers; there are zero failures for orders 1–15 and exactly one at 16, structurally K1 join three K5. Independent exhaustive vertex-subset enumeration confirms all its 65,536 subsets, including d1=1, d2=15, d3=230, and checks all rooted shapes through order 7. The convolution closure theorem eliminates disconnected exceptions. The full script, stdout, and exact recurrence are embedded; no extrapolation or incomplete enumeration is used.

value.rationale: This answers a mathematically motivated minimum-obstruction question: how far logconcavity behavior can be extended from familiar threshold/generalized friendship families to the hereditary trivially perfect graph class. The 2025 primary paper makes an explicit adjacent open query about clique-join logconcavity; its formula alone does not identify the unique smallest failure among every possible rooted-tree structure. A complete natural 16-vertex finite cutoff and uniqueness has value independent of constructing an arbitrary counterexample.
